figures.finding: Greenland levies its own income tax as a flat percentage of taxable income: 10% national (landsskat), 26% or 28% municipal and 6% joint-municipal, so 42% (Qeqertalik, Qeqqata, Sermersooq) or 44% (Avannaata, Kujalleq) in total.
figures.applies: Income year 2026 (the authority's current table). The municipal personal allowance was not read.

figures.finding: The income year is the calendar year; the 2025 return was due by 1 May 2026, so the 2026 return is due 1 May 2027.

sources.said: Et skatteår består af et indkomstår, som varer 12 måneder og som følger kalenderåret.
Selvangivelsen skal indsendes senest 1. maj 2026.

figures.finding: There is no employee social contribution; employers pay a labour-market contribution (AMA) of 1.9% of gross pay in 2026, and employees fully liable in Greenland must pay 11% of A-income into a Greenlandic pension fund.

sources.said: Det betyder, at både private og offentlige arbejdsgivere skal indbetale 1,9 % i AMA i 2026.
All employees subject to full tax liability in Greenland must pay 10% in 2024 (11% in 2025 and onwards) to a Greenlandic pension fund based on the A-tax basis (salaries, etc).

figures.finding: Pay and a freelancer's fee are A-income, taxed provisionally through the tax card; the payer of a performer, artist or author must withhold A-tax, and an employer with no tax card withholds 45%.

Selvstyrets bekendtgørelse siger, at koncerter og optræden beskattes som A-indkomst. Det betyder også, at den der betaler musikeren skal indeholde skat når beløbet udbetales.
akissarsiannit 45 procentimik sulisitsisoq ilanngaasassaaq.

figures.finding: A non-resident with limited liability is taxed on Greenland-source income, including pay for work there (stays over 14 days) and royalties, as a rule at up to 44%; income as an artiste is among it.

sources.said: An individual with limited tax liability to Greenland will, as a main rule, be taxed at up to 44% on income from sources in Greenland.
Certain other types of personal income, including income as an artiste or sportsman, director’s fees, pension distributions

figures.finding: Author's fees, copyright payments and artists' fees are A-income (tax withheld by the payer), while royalties and KODA/GRAMEX payments are B-income; an artist may deduct only the costs of the artistic work. Royalties paid abroad bear 30% withholding unless a treaty reduces it.

Royalties: 30% (may be reduced due to treaty reduction).
There is no VAT in Greenland.
